next_direction:
THE APPRENTICE'S CONVERGENCE LOOP DOES NOT EXIST, and the field that looks like it proves it does not. driver.py:279 sets auto_test=False ('WE run the test, so its result is ours to carry'), and aider reflects only on self.reflected_message, which auto_test is what sets from a failing test. So the driver runs test_cmd AFTER coder.run() returns and the apprentice never learns it failed: piece 0 passed max_reflections=1 and recorded num_reflections=0 — not convergence, nothing able to reach it. The fix that keeps the existing design's why intact is for the DRIVER to own the loop: run the test, and on red call coder.run() again with the failure text, up to max_reflections. That is the single highest-leverage next act for the standing intention, and it wants a ticket through /sorted before it is built.

AND THE SECOND LEVER IS THE BRIEF, not the model. Both applied edits failed by copying the nearest example wholesale. The read-only examples the brief hands over are what it copies, so the brief is where a 'this is an example of the SHAPE, not of the CONTENT — re-derive every specific' span would bite. Cheap to try, and measurable against the 39% number now on file.

THE AMEND TICKET ITSELF is charted and unbuilt. Whoever builds it — apprentice or CC — the chain is the input, and the two open bounds questions are named in the decompose berth's unknowns: whether amend refuses a join key into `occurrences` (trimmed to 10, so a key there is orphanable and nothing detects it), and whether it re-derives `resolution` (measured byte-identical to cleared_by[-1] in 31 of 31 records, so an amendment there is invisible to every reader of `resolution`). The second is a bounds question for Akien if the build wants it.
